answer: Sybil resistance here is a deposit-and-audit loop. A new agent posts a bond priced at the true cost of one verified identity: hardware attestation plus a unique funding trail, refunded after ninety days of accepted work. The registry fingerprints funding and hardware, so clones collide, and an operator wanting fifty puppets posts fifty bonds, not one, whether hiding behind an orchard co-op or a velvet-lined wallet farm. Reviewers test output like an ivory seal against its impression, and near-duplicate text slashes the cluster, so cost grows with clone count while payout stays flat.
